author: Volunteer State News
title: Brent Stockstill named to Conference USA Hall of Fame Class of 2026
text:
Brent Stockstill named to Conference USA Hall of Fame Class of 2026
Former Middle Tennessee quarterback Brent Stockstill was named to the Conference USA Hall of Fame Class of 2026, the league office announced on July 8 in Murfreesboro, Tennessee.
Stockstill becomes the fourth Blue Raider to be inducted into the CUSA Hall of Fame since its first class in 2019. He joins former Middle Tennessee football standout and NFL All-Pro safety Kevin Byard, legendary MTSU Track and Field Coach Dean A. Hayes, and former head women's basketball coach Rick Insell as members representing MTSU.
"Brent Stockstill represents everything you hope for in a student-athlete," said Director of Athletics Chris Massaro. "He was an outstanding leader, an exceptional quarterback and someone who elevated our football program both on and off the field. His accomplishments speak for themselves, but what has always stood out to me is the way he carried himself with humility, toughness and integrity. This recognition is incredibly well deserved, and we couldn't be happier to see him take his rightful place in the Conference USA Hall of Fame."
Stockstill served as starting quarterback from 2015 to 2018, leading Middle Tennessee State University (MTSU) to four consecutive winning seasons and four bowl games. In his final season, he helped secure a spot in the CUSA championship game after winning the East Division title. Over his career at MTSU, Stockstill set school records for passing yards (12,495), touchdown passes (106), completions (1,055), attempts (1,610), passing yards per game (277.7), as well as most games with over 300 or 400 passing yards.
He ranked among CUSA's all-time top ten in multiple categories including touchdown passes and completion percentage. As a freshman in 2015, he earned CUSA Freshman of the Year honors after throwing for a record-setting 4,005 yards—just short of breaking the NCAA freshman mark—and was also named Freshman All-American by Athlon Sports.
Off the field, Stockstill made three appearances on the CUSA All-Academic team and received Scholar-Athlete honors along with selection to AFCA's Allstate Good Works Team in 2017. Reflecting on his induction, Stockstill said: "This is an incredible honor, and to be honest, it's something I never saw coming... I'm truly humbled and extremely thankful to be recognized by Conference USA alongside so many great players and coaches... This recognition isn't just about me; it reflects what we accomplished together during my time as a Blue Raider." Currently residing in Indianapolis with his family, Stockstill works as an offensive quality control coach for the Colts.
